title: Column select (Alt/Option-drag a rectangle of text)
notes: Issue #740. Holding Alt (Option on macOS) when a drag starts selects only the text inside the rectangle drawn, with the Select tool, the text markup tools and Redact (with Highlight and Redact the drag must start on text, since off text they draw an area box). Edit ▸ Column select does the same with a plain drag. A glyph counts when its centre is inside. Copy gives one row per visual line, top to bottom; pieces side by side (table cells) are separated by a tab, right to left in right-to-left rows; vertical text keeps reading order. text_extract takes the same rectangle as rect. Platforms: on Linux desktops whose window manager moves windows with Alt-drag (Xfce, Cinnamon and MATE by default; KDE Plasma 5 and other setups with Alt as the window modifier; GNOME and Plasma 6 use Super) the drag never reaches PdfCraft, so use Edit ▸ Column select or change that setting. On Windows, releasing Alt does not open a system menu (the window has no native menu). The web build has the same Linux caveat in the browser. Checked by hand on Linux (Fedora) with the Column select tool; Alt/Option-drag, and macOS and Windows generally, rest on the kittest tests. Missing: selection across pages, ⇧-click extending a column, a default shortcut, and a check of Acrobat's own copied-text format (not observed).

title: Thumbnail (grid) view of the files before combining
notes: Combine files shows a card per file (the default; Grid/List toggle kept in the settings, --combine-view grid|list): the first page the file contributes (its page range's first page), stacked when it contributes more, and its name shortened in the middle. Cards are sized from 60% to 200% (toolbar slider, buttons and percentage reset, Ctrl/⌘ +/−/0, Ctrl/⌘ with the wheel or a pinch over the grid; kept in the settings, --combine-zoom 60..200), keeping the card under the pointer in place. Hovering a card shows its own actions along the top of its page: remove that file only (whatever else is selected; undoable) and a magnifier that shows the file large, flipping through the pages it adds (buttons, Left/Right; Esc, close or a click outside closes it), also on the card's right-click menu, and Space shows the selected file large (the way there by keyboard). Cards select (click, Ctrl, Shift, arrows by card and by row), drag to reorder (one undo step; the grid scrolls at its edges) and share the list's toolbar. Thumbnails render off the UI thread, only for cards in view, sized to both sides of the page and at most 768 px; at most three render threads at once, counted as threads until they exit (no watchdog replacements; a page stuck for good in one step that can't be interrupted keeps its thread, and so its place, for the rest of the run); textures out of view are dropped over a 32 MB budget (those in view are kept). Locked, unreadable and bad-range files show why instead of a page, and a file whose page size can't be read (e.g. opened with an RC4 owner password) says No preview; page ranges are edited in the list. On the web a thumbnail, and the page shown large, render on the UI thread (one per frame, and only one waits at a time), so a very slow or very large page stalls that frame. A file that adds more than one page (up to 2000) expands into its pages (hover bar, right-click, or Expand all / Collapse all in the toolbar): one card per page it adds, in its range's order, each saying Page N and the file's name, on a tinted band; a click on a page selects that page, Up/Down step rows of cards, dragging a file's card moves the whole file (a drop among a file's pages goes to its nearer end), and its magnifier opens the preview on that page; expanding is a view, not an undo step, and changes nothing in the combined file; a page's render reuses its file's open document for a moment rather than reading the file again. With a file expanded, single pages are selected (click, Ctrl, Shift), dragged anywhere (a page moved between another file's pages splits its file into parts, shown as rows in the list with their own page ranges; parts side by side join again) and removed (a page card's trash, the toolbar, Delete), each one undo step, never changing the files themselves; a split file still counts and combines as one file.

title: Preferences: language
notes: Shortcut modifiers and key names use a dedicated catalog context across toolbar, menus, palette, Help and tooltips, with English fallback and macOS symbols preserved. Preferences switches Auto (system language)/English/Japanese/Simplified Chinese/Traditional Chinese/Czech/Brazilian Portuguese/German/Spanish/French/Telugu/Hungarian/Ukrainian/Italian/Arabic and persists; ui.set language auto|en|ja|zh-hans|zh-hant|cs|pt-br|de|es|fr|te|hu|uk|it|ar and ui.state expose it. TSV catalogs per language (same system as PhotoCraft); every dialog, panel and notice goes through tl!. Japanese, Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, German, Spanish, French and Hungarian cover commands, dialogs, panels, shortcuts and history labels; Czech and Brazilian Portuguese the menus. French locales (fr, fr_FR, fr_CA, fr_BE) select the French catalog, German locales (de, de_DE, de_AT, de_CH) the German one, Hungarian locales (hu, hu_HU) the Hungarian one. German search hints reserve shortcut space, Home cards bound translated text, certificate Subject has its own context, and inserted tool names keep their capitalization. Engine/OS error details stay untranslated. Auto detects the Windows display language after explicitly named supported locale overrides; neutral C/POSIX launcher locales are skipped on Windows, with Chinese script/region mapping and English fallback. Arabic (ar and every ar-* locale) covers commands, dialogs and panels with the six CLDR plural forms; its labels are put into display order when the catalog loads, because egui joins Arabic letters but lays words out left to right. Missing: a right-to-left layout (Arabic labels sit in the left-to-right layout, a wrapped Arabic paragraph breaks at the wrong end, and text typed into a field is not reordered), Czech and Brazilian Portuguese dialogs, Chinese and Telugu font delivery in releases (the pinned craft-fonts revision has an Arabic face; its Noto Sans CJK SC is never embedded, AGENTS.md §1.1), a full localization audit.
